open_points.subject: data_provider — OWNER_FORM_FIELDS
open_points.text:
A row of the owner form table: one field an owner page writes into a form
or a query, and the owner interface reads back (owner, 2026-11-25). The row
gives the field's name, its path in the owner request or its values, with a
tuple's position marked; which of the two it fills; and how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value. A field no row names is not read.
open_points.question: Does each field row apply to every owner route, or where is the relation that says which owner action, page or route may read that field?
options: Add the owner action or route to each field row
Declare every listed field globally admissible on every owner route
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate action-to-field table, keeping field decoding reusable while making each route's accepted fields explicit.

witness.initial: The release contains several owner actions and one OWNER_FORM_FIELDS row whose name and decoding are meaningful for only one of them.
events: The owner submits that field name to a different owner action's route.
outcomes: The reader treats OWNER_FORM_FIELDS as a global whitelist and accepts the field on the different route.
The reader treats fields as route-specific and rejects or ignores it because that route has no declared relation to the row.
witness.observer: The owner sees either an accepted request with the field applied or a refusal/unchanged record.

open_points.subject: models — M29 OwnerFormField
open_points.text:
Facts: the field's name, which holds its path and the mark of each tuple
position in it, so that two rows of different paths are different rows; what
it fills; how its text is read.
open_points.question: What exact reversible and collision-free encoding turns a path and its tuple positions into the field name, and which module owns that encoding and its decoding?
options: Define the complete encoding in the OwnerFormField model
Define a form-name codec module and store its encoded result in each row
Treat each field name as an arbitrary explicit wire string with no derivation from the path
open_points.default_guess: Treat the name as an explicit unique wire string and keep the path and tuple positions as separate structured facts, avoiding an implicit codec.

witness.initial: An owner form contains fields for nested values and repeated tuple positions.
events: The page renderer derives each HTML field name from its path and tuple position.
The reader decodes the submitted names back into request values.
outcomes: One implementer uses dotted paths with numeric components.
Another uses bracketed tuple positions or a different placement of OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK.
witness.observer: The owner sees the submitted value populate a different path, fail to parse, or succeed depending on which renderer and reader implementations are paired.

open_points.subject: data_provider — OWNER_FORM_FIELDS release validity
open_points.text:
No two rows share a name: the name alone
picks a row, and a table in which two rows share one is not a release.
open_points.question: Which module checks this uniqueness condition, at what stage, and with what equality rule, given that models must own no check and data_provider must own no validation?
options: A specification or release validator rejects duplicate names before generation
data_provider validates its table at startup or import time
Consumers detect duplicates when constructing their lookup
open_points.default_guess: Make a release/specification validator the explicit owner and compare field names by exact stored string equality before code generation.

witness.initial: A candidate release contains two OWNER_FORM_FIELDS rows with the same stored name.
events: Generated code loads or constructs the owner-form lookup.
outcomes: A release validator rejects the candidate, so it never becomes a release.
No named validator rejects it; runtime construction keeps the first or last row and the release starts.
witness.observer: The release engineer sees either a build-time rejection or a successful release whose owner interface decodes that field according to one of the duplicate rows.
